token_share.exclusion_rule: Models published under an anonymous or stealth provider are excluded from all share denominators because vendor and licence cannot be established. Their volume is reported above so the effect is visible.

series.note: Weekly vendor lines describe share of the daily top-50 attributed traffic plus the API's aggregate 'other' row, whose vendor mix is not published. When a vendor's model drops out of the daily top 50, its tokens move into 'other' and the vendor's line falls for reasons unrelated to demand — short-run movement can reflect ranking churn rather than usage.

unclassified.note: Not classified: attributed models ranked below the top 50, and the API's aggregate 'other' row, which carries no model identity. Kept in the denominator, never assigned a licence class.

open_weight.method: Licence taken from each model's HuggingFace repository. 'open' means a standard permissive or copyleft licence; 'open-restricted' means weights are published under a bespoke licence with use restrictions; 'unknown' means no public repo matched. Unknown is never collapsed into proprietary.

estimated_spend.label: Estimated routed spend (derived)
assumptions: Tokens multiplied by published list prices from /api/v1/models.
Prompt and completion prices are blended 50/50; the true split is not exposed per model.
List rates only — negotiated enterprise pricing is not public and is typically lower.

Prices are one snapshot of the model registry at fetch time, applied to the whole window. A temporary promotion in force on that day is applied to every day, and earlier or later price changes are not reflected; the registry does not flag promotional prices.

Prompt caching is not modelled. OpenRouter's own weighted-average effective prices sit well below list for input tokens on cache-heavy models, so this estimate overstates what was actually paid for those models.
Covers OpenRouter-routed traffic only, which is a fraction of each vendor's total volume.
This is NOT enterprise spend. It is an estimate of spend on gateway-routed traffic.

task_segmentation.note: Shares are of classified traffic; the unclassified bucket is excluded from the denominator. Data is sampled, so absolute volumes are not available.

known_unknowns.question: Market share across all AI inference
known_unknowns.why: This measures traffic through one gateway. Most enterprise inference goes direct to provider APIs and is invisible here.

known_unknowns.question: Share by industry — financial services, healthcare, legal, manufacturing, public sector, academic and sciences
known_unknowns.why: A routing gateway observes task type, never caller identity. No usage API exposes industry segmentation. Any source publishing these numbers has estimated them.

known_unknowns.question: Enterprise API spend by vendor
known_unknowns.why: No public endpoint exists. The spend figure here is derived from tokens and list prices, covers gateway traffic only, and is not a substitute.

known_unknowns.question: Private and zero-data-retention traffic
known_unknowns.why: OpenRouter's public datasets contain public traffic only. Private models, private endpoints and zero-data-retention requests are excluded at the source, so every share here is a share of public traffic. Enterprise workloads are disproportionately likely to be in the excluded part.

known_unknowns.question: Whether token counts are comparable between vendors
known_unknowns.why: They are not. Each provider's own tokenizer produces the counts, so summing across vendors adds unlike units. Request share is offered as the more comparable measure.

known_unknowns.question: Week-to-week vendor demand
known_unknowns.why: The daily feed lists the top 50 models and folds everything else into one 'other' row whose vendor mix is not published. Weekly vendor lines therefore describe share of top-50 attributed traffic: when a vendor's model falls out of the daily top 50 its line drops for reasons unrelated to demand. Short-run movement can reflect ranking churn rather than usage.
